extracted.intended_audience: Research institutions, CIHR institutes, simulation facilitators, and researchers (trainees to senior) interested in running CIHR Project Grant mock peer review simulations
extracted.subtask_short: CIHR Project Grant mock review simulation
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and templates to design, plan, run, and debrief a mock simulation of the CIHR Project Grant peer review process (three suggested models: Light, Full, Internal). Includes roles, timelines, resources, and adjudication model descriptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose of Peer Review at CIHR
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications are assigned to Reviewers who have, individually or collectively, the required experience and expertise to assess the quality and the potential impact of the proposed research and the research-related activities, within the context of the funding opportunity objectives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PRCs evaluate applications submitted for a particular funding opportunity; rate them on their merit using a defined set of evaluation criteria so they can be ranked by CIHR in order of priority for funding; and make recommendations on the budget needed to support the application. PRCs make recommendations for funding to CIHR and partners, who in turn make the final funding decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: In-person / Teleconference meeting (Project Grant typical)
rubrics_metrics.description: The in-person meeting is typical of the Project Grant competition – Reviewers are assigned applications to review at-home before they convene to discuss and rate the applications via a face-to-face meeting, teleconference, or video conference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used when committee discussion is required; reviewers prepare at-home reviews and then participate in a convened meeting to discuss and rate applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Virtual review (CGRS D typical)
rubrics_metrics.description: The virtual review is typical of the Canada Graduate Research Scholarship – Doctoral (CGRS D) competition – Reviewers complete an electronic, at home review only.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Virtual Reviewers do not discuss applications unless there are sufficient discrepancies in the Reviewers’ scores. Use when discussion is not required or feasible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relevance Review
rubrics_metrics.description: Used when it is important for applications to be relevant to, or in alignment with, targeted research components of the Funding Opportunity (FO).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The relevance review process typically takes place prior to the peer review process. Applications will be assessed using specific criteria and then those deemed relevant will proceed to the next step.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scientific review
rubrics_metrics.description: The standard review mechanism for assessing the scientific excellence of proposals submitted to a competition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Uses a clear set of evaluation criteria to measure key aspects of the proposals in relation to the main scope and objectives of the Funding Opportunity (FO).

rubrics_metrics.name: Merit review
rubrics_metrics.description: A type of review that uses separate scores or ratings for potential impact and scientific merit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In general, the potential impact score of an application reflects the importance of the project to the knowledge-users and the likelihood that it will have a substantive and sustainable impact on health outcomes, practice, programs and/or policy in the study context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Iterative review (Indigenous Health Research focus)
rubrics_metrics.description: A process used in the Project Grant competition to review applications with a central focus on carrying out ethical and culturally competent research involving Indigenous peoples.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications may be reviewed by the Indigenous Health Research (IHR) Committee and may be deemed eligible for the Iterative Peer Review Process, which allows applicants whose applications have been deemed excellent to provide minor clarifications to improve to outstanding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Committee membership selection criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Individual committee members are selected for their knowledge, expertise and/or experience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PRC membership as a whole considers: the need to cover the full range of research areas, relevant methodologies, key populations and experience for which the committee is responsible; the necessity for reviewing capability in both English and French so that applications in either official language can be evaluated by the committee; and the need for regional representation and representation by gender proportionate to membership in the Canadian health research community.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mock Review Toolkit purpose and recommended use
rubrics_metrics.description: The Toolkit was designed to raise awareness of the peer review process at CIHR and help individuals improve their peer review skills and grantsmanship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contains necessary resources to simulate the CIHR Project Grant Peer Review Process, including three suggested simulation models – a Light, Full and Internal simulation model – which can be adapted as required. The Toolkit can stand alone as a peer review resource or be used as a guide to run a mock review simulation or internal peer review process. Users are strongly recommended to read the Toolkit in its entirety prior to running any simulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resources are optional templates
rubrics_metrics.description: Unless otherwise indicated, such as the Conflict of Interest and Confidentiality Agreement, resources referenced throughout the Toolkit are optional templates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Templates serve as suggestions to help support Facilitators during the process. Resources collated include template spreadsheets for logistics and tracking; template invitation emails and promotional materials; conflict of interest and confidentiality agreement templates; pre-simulation training materials and presentations; review templates; SO note template; and mock applications, mock reviews & mock SO notes. A comprehensive list is provided in the Appendix.

rubrics_metrics.name: Facilitator responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: The Facilitator(s) acts as an administrator and is responsible for designing and delivering the simulation from start to finish.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Responsibilities include planning and organizing the simulation, coordinating applications and Reviewers, ensuring that all participants receive necessary pre-simulation training and/or materials, running the Committee meeting proper, and ensuring feedback is collected and collated. The Facilitator(s) can also take on the role of Chair or Scientific Officer if no other person has been appointed to those roles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer responsibilities (mock simulation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers are the primary participant in the mock simulation and are assigned applications to review, score, and present at the face-to-face meeting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers also participate in general committee discussion and provide scores for all other applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chair responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: The committee Chair has the role of moderator during the Committee meeting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It is the Chair’s responsibility to ensure that the review committee functions smoothly, effectively, and objectively. The Chair maintains a positive, constructive, fair-minded environment in which research proposals are evaluated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scientific Officer (SO) responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: The Scientific Officer (SO) is responsible for supporting the Chair in his/her role during the Committee meeting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The SO takes official notes of the committee discussions for each application. The role of SO can also be fulfilled by either the Facilitator or a Reviewer who can switch between roles depending on the application being reviewed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mock review simulation workflow and timeline tasks
rubrics_metrics.description: High-level sequence of tasks across three suggested simulation types (Light, Full, Internal): Selecting a Simulation; Planning the Simulation; Running the Simulation; Post-Simulation activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selecting a Simulation: questionnaire on goals/audience/scope and select simulation type (week 1). Planning: logistics planning, draft high-level timelines, select location, invite facilitator and committee executives, promote simulation, select applications, select and invite reviewers (weeks vary by model). Pre-Simulation: at-home learning, optional training sessions, optional drop-in Q&A. Running: assign applications to Reviewers, send applications, committee meeting agenda and run the meeting (weeks vary). Post-Simulation: debrief and post-simulation survey, and for Internal Simulations provide feedback to Project Grant applicants. The Toolkit maps these tasks to suggested weeks for Light, Full and Internal simulations.
